content.title: About
content.content: Pork and vegetables is a dish where tender pieces of pork are stir‑fried with a variety of vegetables such as bell pepper, zucchini, mushrooms and onion. The recipe excludes carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens, potatoes and soy‑based sauce, making it lighter and suitable for those avoiding these ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide and is rich in protein.
Traditional Asian cuisine often uses soy sauce, but this version replaces it with aromatic herbs and spices.
Vegetables like bell pepper and zucchini are high in vitamin C and antioxidants.
Quick stir‑frying preserves the juiciness of the meat and the crisp texture of the vegetables.
The dish can be easily adapted to different cuisines by changing the spice blend (e.g., adding paprika or ginger).

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork is a good source of B1, B3 and B6 vitamins, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, zinc and selenium, important for immune function and skin health.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell pepper and zucchini contain carotenoids and vitamin C that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Excluding potatoes and soy sauce makes the meal suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Undercooked pork
items.content: Insufficiently cooked pork may harbor harmful bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If soy sauce is replaced with salt, monitor the amount to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to spices used as soy‑sauce alternatives (e.g., mustard).

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Choosing leaner cuts of pork (such as tenderloin) helps reduce overall saturated fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, paired with whole‑grain rice, quinoa, or simply as a standalone meal. Leftover vegetables can be added to a cold salad, or the mixture can be used as a filling for wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pork and vegetables in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, the dish keeps well for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
